author: Codex socialist_green assessment agent (AI-assisted independent assessment)
changeNote: Completed 240 individually interpreted responses and separate substantive evidence review. User authorised neutral representative doctrinal modelling; no 12Axes answers or scores imported.

metadata.name: Social Anarchism (Kropotkinian anarchist communism)
metadata.description: Kropotkinian anarchist communism based on mutual aid, common resources and freely constituted federations without government.
metadata.scope: Kropotkin’s anarchist communism of mutual aid, common productive resources and voluntary interlocking federations. Later wartime positions are outside this doctrinal period. Government is read literally and is not renamed a commune; where both government and capitalist alternatives are rejected the response explicitly records that tension. These survey midpoints do not mean moderate state socialism or market liberalism. This is a representative interpretation, not a questionnaire submitted by adherents. Numeric neutral means a stated mixed/conditional judgement, including rejection of the premise where explained; it is not a claim of measured empirical equivalence. Modern biological and technology items are conditional interpretive judgements where no exact historical position exists; they must not be read as empirical findings or a representative survey of adherents.
metadata.phrase: A society of freely associated communities sharing productive resources and organising cooperation without a coercive state.

sources.title: Kropotkin: Anarchism, Encyclopaedia Britannica 11th edition (1911 transcription)
Kropotkin: Mutual Aid: A Factor of Evolution (1902)
Socialism, especially ownership, Marxist phases and human nature

axes.brief: Kropotkin rejects government and supports free agreements, not selection of a ruling caste. Accountable voluntary delegation is distinct from a national state.
axes.counterEvidence: Anarchist rejection of elected government is not support for autocracy. Conditional neutral items reflect rejection of both state forms rather than absence of research.

answers.rationale: Replacing rulers through elections is preferable to permanence, but national government itself is rejected.
Expert appointment still establishes a ruling authority.
If voting occurs everyone should participate equally, though voting does not legitimise coercion.
Executive legislation against participants’ wishes is imposed rule.
Open political association is supported, while state electoral competition is not the desired institution.
Scrutiny of shared resources is appropriate even though permanent parliamentary offices are not.
Court supremacy and government supremacy both remain state authority.
Union officials should not become a governing caste.
Leaders have no right to prohibit others’ political associations.
Direct participation is welcome but binding state legislation is not voluntary agreement.
Sole national command contradicts freely federated cooperation.
Delegates may be removed, but a constitutional head of government is not retained.
Political continuity cannot entitle someone to perpetuate rule.
Recallable delegation fits participant control better than fixed unaccountable office.
Unaccountable leadership is incompatible with anarchism.
Military judgement cannot legitimise a new governing authority.

axes.brief: Freedom from punishment-based obedience and state hierarchy supports personal autonomy and opposition to coercive police powers.
axes.counterEvidence: Kropotkin explicitly includes mutual protection among voluntary functions. Opposing police does not mean indifference to harm or refusal of all self-defence.

answers.rationale: Autonomous adults should make self-regarding choices without state punishment.
A court order does not eliminate the coercive character of state surveillance.
Peaceful direct action should not depend on official permission.
Criticism is essential to free association.
Coercive paternalism contradicts self-direction.
Police tracking is precisely the state supervision rejected.
Shared safety should use voluntary arrangements rather than suspicionless coercive stops.
Predictive state restraint is incompatible with no-government freedom.
Moral officials have no authority to censor adults’ access.
Communication should not be conditional on state identification.
General police searches impose authority on innocent individuals.
Official prohibition replaces voluntary protection with command.
Warrants constrain existing police, but neither warranted nor arbitrary state search is the ideal.
Disclosure enables people to resist coercive misconduct.
Voluntary mutual defence is compatible with personal defensive arms.
Indefinite detention is a direct form of domination.

axes.brief: Freely constituted associations permit many cultures and ways of life; no nation should impose cultural uniformity.
axes.counterEvidence: The source contains dated ethnographic terminology; this does not authorise racial hierarchy or modern claims of biological group differences.

answers.rationale: No national cultural authority should override voluntary communities.
Accommodation is valuable but compulsory public spending is not the anarchist mechanism.
Settlement should not require cultural obedience.
Distinct identities can participate in free associations.
Useful shared languages and diverse service languages can be chosen voluntarily.
Recognition can respect historically displaced communities without national command.
State cultural preference perpetuates imposed hierarchy.
Neither collective identity should override free individual association.
Imposing one calendar conflicts with freely chosen community practices.
Cultural plurality is welcome but official national identity is not necessary.
Voluntary wider participation is useful, imposed integration programmes are not.
Locally useful multilingual signs facilitate free cooperation.
National identity should not be prescribed as superior to community ties.
Both general bans and special legal exceptions presuppose coercive clothing regulation.
Several cultural ways of life can coexist in common territory.
Official cultural conversion conflicts with freely formed communities.

axes.brief: Voluntary association across borders opposes state immigration restrictions and labour-market gatekeeping.
axes.counterEvidence: No state is an incumbent implementation of a no-government doctrine. Practical cooperative capacity is different from official admission quotas.

answers.rationale: National quotas impose state control over movement.
People may freely seek a place to live and cooperate.
Skills tests subordinate membership to productive usefulness.
Free family association should cross territorial borders.
Assistance should not be withheld for lacking skills or cultural similarity.
State migration illegality should not justify expulsion.
Employer demand does not justify a coercive ceiling on people.
Common housing problems should be addressed cooperatively rather than by exclusion.
Family movement should not depend on a state numerical ceiling.
Work cooperation can support moving, though an employer offer is not required.
Sponsorship turns free movement into dependence on a gatekeeper.
University credentials neither create nor extinguish a free right of movement.
Mutual aid supports refuge irrespective of official quotas.
Cultural-origin preference contradicts open free association.
Common provision includes newcomers, but a welfare-state citizenship distinction is not retained.
Difference itself should not grant preferential entitlement over others.

axes.brief: Territorial mutual defence appears among voluntary associations; imperial armies and coercive national mobilisation do not.
axes.counterEvidence: The scope ends in 1910. Kropotkin’s later support for the Allied war effort is not silently blended into the earlier anarchist account.

answers.rationale: National interests cannot authorise coercive foreign campaigns.
Peaceful agreement fits the preferred method of resolving conflict.
Military superiority recreates centralised state power.
Immediate mutual defence can be legitimate, but state preemptive-war authority is not.
Voluntary defence need not follow the categories of national states and allies.
Compulsory male national service contradicts free agreement.
Compromise should ordinarily preserve peaceful cooperation.
Autonomous national killing systems intensify unaccountable coercion.
Mutual territorial defence is preferable to expeditionary war.
Mutual protection can involve resistance, so avoidance at every cost is too absolute.
Prolonged national expeditionary forces contradict free federation.
A territorial dispute should not become a war of rulers.
Military threats are coercion rather than voluntary agreement.
War prevention outweighs demonstrations of state resolve.
Competitive state espionage sustains militarised antagonism.
Negotiated demilitarisation can reduce coercive power.

axes.brief: Federations can be local, regional, national and international, but remain voluntary rather than binding sovereign authorities.
axes.counterEvidence: International cooperation does not mean international compulsion. Several neutral items distinguish free federations from both sovereign options.

answers.rationale: National institutions have no ultimate right to command association.
International institutions likewise lack coercive authority over unwilling people.
Neither national nor international sovereign courts are the preferred dispute mechanism.
Durable federations are possible, but enforced national alliances are not voluntary.
Voluntary association includes freedom to withdraw from imposed commitments.
Accountability is important without establishing binding sovereign international courts.
National advantage should not override freely agreed common purposes.
Environmental coordination is necessary but should be federative rather than coercive.
Voluntary common policy is possible without compulsory state-bloc membership.
Human freedom matters but international legal command is not itself anarchist.
Both sovereign national currency and sovereign international monetary control are rejected.
Shared resources and decisions can be voluntarily pooled.
Exclusive national control over borders conflicts with free association.
Common agreements can facilitate distribution but state trade rules are not the ideal.
Voluntary international federation is supported, permanent political state authority is not.
Voluntary common protection differs from coercive enforcement of interstate rules.

axes.brief: Common productive resources replace capitalist monopoly and state ownership alike. Public/private binary items frequently fit neither.
axes.counterEvidence: Kropotkin criticises state socialism as well as private monopoly; the IEP ownership distinction prevents relabelling common ownership as government property.

answers.rationale: Capitalist productive monopoly contradicts common resources.
Common utilities are neither state enterprises nor capitalist networks.
Comparable outcomes do not justify restoring capitalist ownership.
State businesses and capitalist competition both differ from free common production.
Capitalist healthcare ownership conflicts with common access.
Railways can be commonly coordinated without government ownership.
Cheap private contracts still reproduce capitalist control of work.
Public-private banking coexistence is not the means of common provisioning.
Selling shared production to capitalists contradicts anarchist communism.
Common shelter is neither public-body landlordism nor private rental property.
Government regulation cannot make capitalist strategic ownership the preferred system.
Common resources are not synonymous with state-owned extraction firms.
Routine capitalist contracts replace free common provision with private profit.
Neither government retention nor privatisation describes voluntary common property.
Capitalist sale is no solution to problems of common production.
Communications should be freely organised rather than confined to state or private owners.

axes.brief: International free cooperation is desirable but capitalist buying, selling and investment are not the desired organisation of production.
axes.counterEvidence: Free agreements are not identical to unrestricted capitalist investor rights. The assessment does not infer economic liberalism from absence of tariffs.

answers.rationale: Tariffs impose state privilege for domestic capital.
Free cooperation is supported but capitalist trade liberalisation is not the complete alternative.
Supplier nationality does not warrant state purchasing preference.
Free sourcing can aid cooperation, but capitalist firms’ rights are not the ideal’s basis.
National import restrictions are coercive means of organising essential supply.
Removing state barriers can widen voluntary cooperation, without endorsing capitalist exchange.
State trade privilege for new capitalist industries contradicts free common production.
Both domestic and foreign capitalist investment are superseded by common control.
Local food resilience should be built through cooperation rather than compulsory import exclusion.
Neither protected capital nor unprotected capital embodies common production.
Retaliatory tariffs reproduce state rivalry.
Equal and discriminatory state product taxes are both coercive fiscal arrangements.
Another state’s subsidy is not a reason for coercive trade restrictions.
Voluntary international exchange differs from treaties managing national tariff powers.
Neither domestic nor foreign capitalist control of common resources is acceptable.
Cross-border access to services should not face special state barriers.

axes.brief: Voluntary coordination of production replaces both state command and capitalist competition; neither government nor commune is silently substituted in the questions.
axes.counterEvidence: Social planning can occur without government compulsory output schedules. Bank, currency and wage questions may presuppose institutions this variant abolishes.

answers.rationale: Freedom from government is supported, private capitalist control is not.
Compulsory government output targets directly contradict free agreements.
Government price-setting and capitalist market allocation both differ from needs-based sharing.
National government investment direction is not voluntary coordination.
Neither capitalist demand nor government production commands should govern common work.
Common access to essentials supersedes both state prices and private seller power.
Freedom of initiative is supported, capitalist firms and licensing are both rejected.
State-directed bank credit is part of the authority being replaced.
Freedom from state approval does not endorse the capitalist monetary institutions presupposed.
Subsidies steering private industry sustain both government and capital.
Freedom of association does not require competing private currencies in anarchist communism.
Wage abolition is preferred to either a legal wage floor or unrestricted employer bargaining.
Free producers organise work without capitalist wages or government schedules.
Central-bank direction is not the freely federated production envisaged.
Market rents turn common shelter into private monopoly.
Government coordination is not substituted for the voluntary coordination actually supported.

axes.brief: Need-based common provision replaces wage dependence and compulsory fiscal redistribution; social abundance is not a modest welfare floor.
axes.counterEvidence: Redistribution scores can mislead because both taxation and private wage accumulation are rejected; need-based sharing is stated in the brief instead of manipulating answers.

answers.rationale: Common needs-based sharing differs from government taxes on private earnings.
Compulsory taxation is rejected, but retaining unequal capitalist income is also rejected.
A common social minimum is supported without a state tax-benefit mechanism.
Common abundance should exceed a minimal safety net.
Progressive taxation remains a state mechanism rather than common provisioning.
Private earnings claims cannot govern distribution of common resources.
Inheritance of productive monopoly is rejected rather than made a continuing tax base.
Common support follows need rather than state benefit time limits.
Taxing private wealth is not the same as abolishing its productive monopoly.
Lower burdens on private taxpayers are not the criterion for meeting needs.
Common provisioning should enable a rich social life.
Tax cuts and benefit expansion both presume fiscal state institutions.
Wage supplements retain an employer system the doctrine supersedes.
Neither flat nor graduated state income-tax schedules define need-based distribution.
Common land differs from compensated subdivision into individual property.
Need-based common provision extends beyond preventing starvation.

axes.brief: Critique of church-state domination is compatible with voluntary beliefs and excludes clerical power over common life.
axes.counterEvidence: Criticism of institutional religion does not imply that a coercive state should suppress private faith.

answers.rationale: Common decisions should rest on human judgement rather than religious commands.
Religious law is another imposed authority.
No cleric should approve decisions on behalf of everyone.
A faith-founded state is incompatible with no-government association.
Open learning can examine religion without conversion.
Official religious cultivation infringes intellectual autonomy.
State courts and religious courts are both imposed institutions, neither is the anarchist ideal.
Clerical review gives special people authority over others.
Common gatherings should not impose worship.
Compulsory funds should not spread religious obedience.
Shared institutions should not endorse one compulsory creed.
Voluntary festivals can persist without state recognition of religious superiority.
A religious title grants no right to govern.
Special tax privilege and the underlying compulsory tax apparatus are both rejected.
Personal unions need no religious permission.
Binding religious family commands contradict voluntary personal association.

axes.brief: Free individual development and opposition to hierarchy support changing imposed customs, without prescribing all future intimate arrangements.
axes.counterEvidence: Kropotkin’s freedom principle is stronger than evidence for any particular modern marriage or abortion rule; qualified responses avoid fabricated specific advocacy.

answers.rationale: Freely evolving associations should adapt customs as participants change.
Longevity cannot justify imposing a custom on unwilling people.
Household variation is compatible with free individual development.
Obligatory sex roles impose social hierarchy.
Free same-sex unions are compatible with autonomy, while state marriage licensing is not retained.
One household model should not command social conformity.
Bodily self-direction supports acceptance of an adult’s early-pregnancy choice as an inference.
Children’s free development should not be monopolised by parental traditionalism.
Parenting should be judged through care rather than an imposed sex norm.
Inherited modesty rules cannot bind everyone.
Voluntary language change can respect how people understand themselves.
Free learning should not prioritise inherited obedience.
Unconventional adult roles deserve equal freedom and acceptance.
Popular voluntary change need not wait for guardians of tradition.
Free education can explain different sexual and gender lives.
Harmless customs may survive voluntarily, without an obligation to preserve them.

axes.brief: Kropotkin values technological capacity to shorten burdensome labour, but decentralised life and social usefulness constrain its application.
axes.counterEvidence: Technical optimism is not evidence of a historically documented view on AI or gene editing. Each answer is a bounded present-day application.

answers.rationale: Useful technical advances can increase free time with proportionate safeguards.
Some trials are prudent but blanket long-term delay conflicts with technical possibility.
Infrastructure benefits and local ecological costs require agreement among those affected.
Voluntary informed use requires adequate safety knowledge.
Common ownership can turn automation into reduced toil rather than unemployment.
Local ecological continuity matters alongside shared material needs.
New food methods warrant open experimentation informed by environmental evidence.
Irreversible elective implants merit careful safety study.
Technical improvement should accompany changed production and consumption.
Affected communities should understand ecological effects before irreversible building.
Adult autonomy supports use, while uncertain irreversible harms support caution.
Reliable evidence protects recipients of freely organised healthcare.
Scientific experimentation and the autonomy of future persons require a conditional judgement.
Ecological knowledge should inform widespread crop changes.
Shelter and mobility are real needs without a universal entitlement to destroy undeveloped land.
Irreversible harms deserve strong evidence before common adoption.

axes.brief: Voluntary federations reject national supremacy and coercive regional states alike; coordination varies with the task.
axes.counterEvidence: Voluntary national-scale coordination is explicitly possible, so localism does not mean isolated self-sufficient villages or rejection of disaster coordination.

answers.rationale: Local autonomy is valuable, but sovereign regional governments are not substituted for the state.
A national final say contradicts voluntary federation.
Voluntary association must allow communities to leave, with minority freedom protected.
National override is coercive rule even when its programme has benefits.
Communities can choose structures, but regional state constitutions remain a qualified premise.
A single national police command exemplifies central domination.
Local or national compulsory taxation is not the distribution method proposed.
National curriculum command restricts freely organised learning.
Regional tax autonomy and national taxation are both state institutions.
Shared labour norms can be freely agreed, but national employment law is not the mechanism.
Participants should shape local associations without higher-state permission.
A national healthcare decree cannot replace free collective provision.
Indigenous communities should organise affairs through their own free institutions.
State tax competition and national enforcement are both outside anarchist communism.
Locally contained ecological affairs should be handled by those affected.
Cross-region coordination is desirable but national command against local consent is not.

axes.brief: Mutual Aid treats cooperation as an evolved tendency developed through institutions and experience; it is expressly not a purely cultural blank slate.
axes.counterEvidence: Cooperation’s evolutionary basis is counter-evidence against equating anarchism with culture-only causation. No empirical estimate of IQ or racial heritability is imputed.

answers.rationale: Kropotkin combines evolved social instincts with institutions that develop or suppress them.
His evolutionary account and historical learning do not justify a national IQ causal hierarchy.
Social constraints shape roles while an evolutionary account retains embodied influences.
Bodily susceptibility and difficult environments jointly matter to stress.
Freedom and opportunities enable varied interests to develop.
Instinctive disposition and experience can both shape risk behaviour.
Mutual aid is both an evolved disposition and an institutionally cultivated habit.
Sympathy has evolutionary roots while its expression develops socially.
Natural capacities and educational surroundings both affect attention.
Evolved social instincts and customary moral learning both influence immediate judgement.
Natural defensive responses and learned threats can operate together.
Individual dispositions and the social setting jointly shape temperament.
Embodied attraction and cultural variation are compatible with his developmental account.
His emphasis on cooperation across societies challenges a racial inherited-violence account.
Learned mutual responsibility is a better account than racialised self-control.
Gendered exclusion and work organisation can shape earnings rather than inherent differences in productive contribution alone.

review.notes: Read all 240 answers against the current question wording and checked values, rationales, cited source IDs and axis distinctions. Checked Kropotkin’s Britannica text, Mutual Aid and SEP/IEP. The primary text explicitly rejects handing railways, mines and banks to the state: retained the distinction between voluntary common property and government ownership. Audited every fiscal and planning premise and the noncoercive-federation qualifications. Retained the mixed Culture axis because evolved cooperation is part of Kropotkin’s argument. Updated ebook and SEP revision dates; no real government is presented as the anarchist ideal. All answers remain labelled inferred: these are scoped representative models, not claimed questionnaire responses or empirical measurements of adherents. Review used no target scores or similarity tuning. Similarity audit remains the catalogue coordinator’s separate step.
